subject: health
title: Hop, Skip and Jump
about: The PE words for hopping, skipping, sliding, galloping, leaping, dribbling, striking and kicking, and the movement ideas of pathways, levels, speed, general space, the beat and using the teacher's tip. NC Grade 1 PE motor skills and movement concepts (PE.1.MS.1, PE.1.MC.2); a vocabulary deck, the real practice happens in PE and at the park.
tip: Call out hop, skip, slide and gallop and let him do each one across the room before he answers.

cards.q: Stand on one foot and bounce up and down on that foot. What move is that?
cards.note: A hop takes off on one foot and lands on that same foot.

cards.q: You bounce along with a step and a hop, switching feet each time. What move is that?
cards.note: A skip is a step and a hop on one foot, then a step and a hop on the other.

cards.q: To move sideways across the gym, step out and bring your feet together. What move is that?
cards.note: To slide, step to the side, bring your other foot to meet it, and step again.

cards.q: Which move is like a horse running, with the same foot always in front?
cards.note: In a gallop the same foot stays in front the whole time.

cards.q: What do we call jumping off one foot and landing on the other foot?
cards.note: A leap takes off on one foot and lands on the other foot.

cards.q: A basketball player pushes the ball down so it bounces back up, again and again. What is that called?
cards.note: Push the ball down with your fingertips so it bounces back up to you.

cards.q: In baseball or tennis, you swing and hit the ball. What is that called?
cards.note: You can strike a ball with a bat, a paddle or your hand.

cards.q: Which part of your body do you kick a ball with?
cards.note: Plant one foot next to the ball and kick with the other foot.

cards.q: A friend tosses you a ball. To catch it, what do you keep your eyes on?
cards.note: Watch the ball all the way into your hands.

cards.q: When you throw a ball, which way do you step?
cards.note: Step with the foot opposite your throwing hand, toward where you want the ball to go.

cards.q: You can move along a straight line, a curvy line or a zigzag. These lines are called what?
cards.note: A pathway is the line you make as you move. A zigzag goes sharp one way, then the other.

cards.q: You can crawl down low, walk at medium height or stretch up high. Those are three what?
cards.note: Low is down near the floor. High is up by your head or higher.

cards.q: You can tiptoe slowly or run fast. Slow and fast are two kinds of what?
cards.note: Speed is how fast or how slow you move.

cards.q: What do we call all the room you can move in during PE?
cards.sayQ: What do we call all the room you can move in during P E class?
cards.note: Personal space is just the bubble around you. General space is the whole room.

cards.q: What do we call moving the same way the hands on a clock turn?
cards.note: Clock hands go to the right across the top. The other way is counterclockwise.

cards.q: The drum goes boom, boom, boom and you stomp with every boom. What are you stomping to?
cards.note: The beat is the steady pulse in music that you can clap to.

cards.q: Your coach says, step toward your target when you throw. What do you do with that tip?
cards.note: A tip from your teacher is called feedback. Using it helps you get better.
